# Why the fingerprint check fails on this ticket, and what it is not

The sixth triage, record 84, and the seventh, record 86, both refuse the
fingerprint: check 80's regression ran against `2c17ec1dff35` and the triage
reads `454ecfca39d7`. The commit that recorded the qa check blamed
`repository.fingerprint` for reading blob ids out of the index, and implied the
check measures something it should not. That was wrong, and this note is the
correction.

**The evidence that it was wrong.** SEEN-107 ran eleven triages and the
fingerprint check passed in every one of them, against the same code. A check
that eleven consecutive triages satisfy is not a check that cannot be satisfied.

**What actually caused it, both halves mine.** The first is ordering. The
procedure says the outcome is written before the ticket leaves review, and the
fingerprint compares the tree against the last tdd check; this session wrote the
outcome after the regression, so the tree moved between them. Written before the
final red, green and regression, as SEEN-107 wrote it, the regression runs
against the tree that carries it and the fingerprint matches. The second is
staging. `git ls-files -s` reports the index, so a tracked file edited and not
staged hashes as its old content and staging it moves the fingerprint without
changing a byte on disk; running the final checks on a committed tree, which is
what SEEN-107 did, leaves nothing to move.

**What stands in its place here.** Check 85 is the whole suite, 820 tests,
recorded at the review stage against the tree the reviewer reads, which is the
tree the receipt will attest. It cannot make the fingerprint check pass, because
that check reads only the red, green and regression of the tdd stage, and the
tdd stage is behind us at record 82. So the failure is carried to the reviewer
rather than answered, which forces full depth, and full depth is right for a
ticket whose tree moved after its tests.

**What to do next time, and it is a habit rather than a change.** Write the
outcome, commit, then run the final red, green, regression and coverage, then
advance. The harness already reads that order; this session did not.
